fixes.explanation: That's them, friend. The angel says those who dwell on the earth “…whose names were not written in the Book of Life from the foundation of the world will marvel when they see the beast…” (Revelation 17:8) That's who does the marveling. And what they marvel at is the beast.

Right, it's false. Of the seven kings, the one who has not yet come “…must remain for only a little while.” (Revelation 17:10) The angel says he comes, and then his stay is short. The passage doesn't give a number, so a little while is the whole answer.

Refreshed sounds like a nice day off with a cool breeze. That's not what the angel says. He says those who dwell on the earth were “…intoxicated with the wine of her immorality.” (Revelation 17:2) Intoxicated is the word, friend.

Nourished sounds like something that does you good. The angel picks a different word for this wine. Those who dwell on the earth were “…intoxicated with the wine of her immorality.” (Revelation 17:2) The word is intoxicated, friend.
Right, it's false. The text says the scarlet beast was “…covered with blasphemous names…” (Revelation 17:3) That's not a name tag anybody would want.

Nineveh is the city Jonah was sent to preach to (Jonah 1:2). It's a real city in the Bible, but it's not the one on her forehead. The name starts with “BABYLON THE GREAT…” (Revelation 17:5) Good thinking, friend, Nineveh just isn't the city named there.
It's true. The whole name reads “BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” (Revelation 17:5) The name goes on past the city, and every word of it is there.

Destruction is the word. The beast “…is about to come up out of the Abyss and go to its destruction.” (Revelation 17:8) Big entrance, rough exit. The angel says it again a few verses later, that the beast “…is going into destruction.” (Revelation 17:11)

Not this one, friend. The angel never says the ones who marvel are those who follow the Lamb. He says it's those “…whose names were not written in the Book of Life from the foundation of the world…” (Revelation 17:8) Later in the passage, the Lamb's people are called “…called and chosen and faithful…” (Revelation 17:14)

One would make the beast the first king, but the angel counts it differently. He lists seven kings (Revelation 17:10), and says the beast “…is an eighth king, who belongs to the other seven…” (Revelation 17:11) So it comes in at number eight, friend.

True. The angel says the ten kings “…will make war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will triumph over them…” (Revelation 17:14) Ten kings, a war, and the Lamb still triumphs. The story isn't over yet, though, so there's more to come.

That's how the angel explains it. “The waters you saw, where the prostitute was seated, are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues.” (Revelation 17:15) So no swimming gear needed. The waters are a list of peoples, multitudes, nations and tongues.

No idol is mentioned in the angel's answer. He says, “And the woman you saw is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth.” (Revelation 17:18) The city is the one doing the ruling over the kings.
